subject: Electrical Engineering
title: HVDC: Direct Current Comes Back
description: A short lesson to help you apply HVDC: Direct Current Comes Back.

hook.text: Edison lost the current war, but DC is making a comeback for long-distance lines.

buildup.text: HVDC converts AC to DC, transmits it, then converts back at the other end.

discovery.text: DC has no reactive power losses and needs fewer conductors than AC.

twist.text: Undersea cables must use HVDC — AC leaks too much energy through cable capacitance.

climax.text: China's Changji–Guquan HVDC link runs 3,293 km at 1,100 kV DC.

punchline.text: For very long distances, DC beats AC after all.

quiz.question: Why is HVDC preferred for undersea power cables?
options: Saltwater blocks AC but conducts DC
AC loses too much energy through cable capacitance in long underwater runs
DC cables are lighter and float better underwater
